name: repro_package
description: Generate final_provenance/, the folder that reproduces a run for someone else, and prove it in a clean shell; generic apps and flux-batch apps (Elmerfold) with a per-chunk moirai wrapper; then publish the verified package and its traces (baseline + in-place verification) to a shared group root with group permissions. The standalone prov_check.py verifies activities, entity types and dangling ids, and counts entities/edges only informationally when the run captures run-dependent values. Load for the package stage, for 'publish', 'provenance-repro', 'provenance-traces', 'chgperm', '/p/vast1/moirai', 'prov_check', 'entities: N, the original run had M', or when a package ran the service on the login node, the batch job was never waited for, or a chunk job failed unnoticed.

history.why: from dftracer-agents' planner and reproduction packages

repro_build's generic package cannot reproduce Elmerfold: it started moirai-service on the login node and eval'd the pipeline's multi-step command ending in an async `flux batch` (compute nodes have no service, no wrapper, no annotated --src-dir, no smoke input, nothing waits or validates). Adds a `batch` mode (auto-detected from the baseline/moirai_smoke outputs or `mode`): per-chunk wrapper written from a template, run.sh generated by the app's gen_launch_script.py, one flux batch, flux watch, failure checks on the batch --output and hosts.txt (same logic as moirai_run's batch wrapper job), no service on the login node. repro_verify supports it. Generic mode unchanged. New pure tools repro_batch_render and repro_batch_selftest (fake flux/module/python in a temp dir, nothing on the cluster).

repro_build's generic package cannot reproduce flux-batch apps (Elmerfold): it starts moirai-service on the login node and evals an asynchronous multi-step COMMAND with unreplaced placeholders. Adds a batch mode (per-chunk wrapper starts the service on the worker, generated run.sh, flux batch + watch, failure scan, smoke input), batch-aware repro_verify, and sandbox selftests that run the real 04_run.sh with stub flux/python.

repro_build's generic package cannot reproduce Elmerfold: 04_run started moirai-service on the login node and ran the pipeline's multi-step command ending in an asynchronous flux batch (no service on compute nodes, wrapper and annotated copy unused, no 2-sequence smoke input, nothing waited for or validated the batch). Adds a batch mode (auto-detected or explicit) with per-chunk wrapper template, run.sh generation, flux batch + watch + chunk-failure checks, a batch-aware repro_verify, and a pure sandbox selftest. Generic mode unchanged.

The package stage ends in the repo's local folder; people need it published like /p/vast1/dftracer-user/moirai: provenance-repro/<app>/ (the package, verified by running it AS IT IS from the published folder in a clean login shell) and provenance-traces/<app>/<job start>/ (baseline and verification runs with README/run.json/run.sh/graph_summary.json made from tool counts), then group permissions through the site's chgperm.sh. Adds repro_publish_plan (dry run), repro_publish_package, repro_publish_traces, repro_publish_permissions, repro_publish_validate, repro_publish_selftest, repro_verify(in_place=...), and repro_validate checks the published tree when one was recorded.

Publishing for the package stage, rebased on live v4 (check_batch.py, submit_moirai.sh.tmpl, parse_gen/_batch_cfg, moirai_venv in repro_verify, no_login_service). Adds repro_publish_plan (dry run), repro_publish_package, repro_publish_traces, repro_publish_permissions, repro_publish_validate, repro_publish_selftest and repro_verify(in_place=...) so the package runs as it is from the published folder in a clean login shell and leaves a verification record; repro_validate checks the published tree when one was recorded. All v4 tools are kept (repro_build, repro_verify, repro_validate, repro_batch_selftest).

Consolidation: repro_package is the home of the generic package and publish procedure. It gains the two generic items workload_biotox_repro held alone (polling a long repro_verify, the job-id lint word), and says the copy-mode check is optional (skipped for BioTox). workload_biotox_repro now points here instead of repeating the config.ini, no-overwrite, OUTPUT_ROOT and .chgperm_logs rules.

Live Run view: publish a live run's data (publish_data stage). repro_publish_traces on a live pipeline publishes its live_run traces as kind 'live' (publish_root and app from the parent's published package; run.sh from the run's script), recorded on publish_data; repro_publish_data_validate checks files, run files and counts.

Defect (measured): since the annotation captures run inputs and attributes (command lines, self.* fields, ctx pointers, gpu devices), entity and edge counts of a run are not deterministic (two identical baseline runs: 1079 and 1184 entities, same 190 activities and types). prov_check.py compared activities, entities and edges for exact equality, so the in-place verification of the published package failed on 'entities: 393, the original run had 58' with nothing wrong. Fix: repro_build stores the sorted entity TYPES of the reference traces in expected.json; prov_check.py requires equal activities, every expected type present (extras allowed) and no dangling id, and treats entity/edge counts as informational (counts, expected, note) when an expected type ends with .input or .attribute; old expected.json without types keeps the exact comparison. The verification record never lists entity/edge count differences in that case. New validator repro_check_selftest reproduces it.

Queries on a published run were slow: nothing indexed the published traces, so the first query built a TraceViewer index file by file (minutes for a 31-file, 2.8 GB live run). repro_publish_traces now builds raw/.dftindex in the published folder on all cores, after the final rename (the index is keyed by absolute path: the run's own .dftindex is no longer copied, it would be rebuilt anyway), with group bits = user bits; an index failure is returned as index.error without undoing the publish. New repro_publish_index backfills folders published before (every app when app is empty). publish_checks and repro_publish_data_validate require the index. Selftest: index built in the published folder, run index not copied, index failure keeps the publish, per-folder errors reported.

User feedback (process): "verification should never happen on home. It should happen on lustre or workspace". repro_verify(in_place=<elmerfold-v10>) failed 4 times with OSError Errno 122 Disk quota exceeded writing <OUTPUT_ROOT>/verification.json: OUTPUT_ROOT came from repro_build's default ${HOME}/moirai_repro/${APP} and /g/g92 (24 GB quota) was full; a failed pip build left a 41 MB half-built moirai-venv. Step 1 of 2: the rule in the skill; the tool change follows by capability_refine.

Step 2 (tool + unit check) of the user feedback "verification should never happen on home. It should happen on lustre or workspace". Evidence: repro_verify(in_place=<elmerfold-v10>) failed 4 times with OSError Errno 122 Disk quota exceeded writing <OUTPUT_ROOT>/verification.json (OUTPUT_ROOT from repro_build default ${HOME}/moirai_repro/${APP}; /g/g92 24 GB full; a failed pip build left a 41 MB moirai-venv). Changes: repro_verify output_root (in-place: a home OUTPUT_ROOT is overridden through env OUTPUT_ROOT to /p/lustre5/$USER/moirai_repro/<app> if writable else <workspace>/verification/<app>, recorded in overrides; explicit wins but is refused on home; copy mode refuses isolation_root on home); repro_build default output_root /p/lustre5/${USER}/moirai_repro/${APP} (else workspace path), portable; _verification_record builds the record in memory and returns status error naming path, df and fix on OSError; new repro_home_selftest and its check. SKILL.md is already v11.

Step 2 (tool change) of the user's feedback "verification should never happen on home. It should happen on lustre or workspace" (4 x Errno 122 writing verification.json, OUTPUT_ROOT from repro_build default ${HOME}/moirai_repro/${APP}, home 24 GB full). repro_verify gets output_root: in-place overrides a home OUTPUT_ROOT through the env (OUTPUT_ROOT=...) to /p/lustre5/$USER/moirai_repro/<app> when writable else <workspace above the session>/verification/<app>, recorded in overrides; an explicit output_root wins but is refused on home; isolation_root on home is refused. repro_build default output_root is /p/lustre5/${USER}/moirai_repro/${APP} (else a workspace path), portable. _verification_record builds the record in memory, mkdirs the output folder, returns status error naming path, df and fix on OSError, and status outputs_gone when the earlier run's folder (run.json, work/) was removed (the user deleted /g/g92/haridev/moirai_repro); repro_verify then starts a fresh batch instead of waiting for the old job. New unit check repro_home_selftest (resolved default root does not start with home). Skill rule is already live in v11.

The user's rule: every capability reads traces only through TraceViewer, never by decompressing or parsing the trace files. prov_check.py now reads the traces with dftracer.utils.TraceViewer (same counts as before on the openfold baseline: 220 activities, 1564 entities, 5026 edges); 02_setup_env always installs dftracer-utils; 05_validate runs the checker with the moirai venv's python.

repro_publish_validate and repro_publish_data_validate rebuilt the whole provenance graph (provtrace.read: every record a Python object, 16 workers, 19.6 GB) to compare three counts: 8+ min on elmerfold-v10 (8.08M entities, 39.2M edges), ~20 min and cut for a live run (lessons L-37724d70, L-1087f2c9). Now run.json records a size+sha256 manifest of the counted trace files and the validators check the published files against it (0.4 s on elmerfold-v10); folders published before manifests are checked by file count and bytes; deep=true keeps the full recount.
One reader: index_raw builds the published index through prov_read (core.provtrace.ensure_index), not dftracer.utils.

User (going to sleep): "validate everything, fix anything that is needed and then publish this version of elmerfold for querying". Finding: repro_build wrote patches/provenance.patch from only ann["files"] (3 files for Elmerfold) plus _moirai_prov.py, so after the dftracer performance annotation (python_annotate_project on 31 files, rewritten to `from moirai import ...`) the published package lacks 28 annotated files and a reproduction runs without most of the performance annotation. Rule: the patch holds every text file that differs between the pristine source and the annotated copy. Skill part first (tool_code follows in a refinement).

User: every tool should use the dftracer pre-release with its prebuilt modules and compose as needed. A package now installs the pre-release the run used with dftracer-modules at the same version (a git spec still builds from source), then compose_dftracer (in lib_load_config.sh) composes the modules the run had linked, recorded by PIN as dftracer-composition and written to config.ini as DFTRACER_MODULES (empty: MPI and HDF5). repro_install_selftest runs compose_dftracer in bash for each case.
